title: Primetime: A Drama That Puts the Media in Focus
seoTitle: Primetime: Robert Pattinson Stars as Chris Hansen
subtitle: Robert Pattinson plays Chris Hansen in Lance Oppenheim's feature debut
excerpt: The film 'Primetime', which premiered at the Venice Film Festival, stars Robert Pattinson as controversial host Chris Hansen, recounting the years of 'To Catch a.'
author: Daniele Morais
contentHtml:
The highlight of the Venice Film Festival was Lance Oppenheim's debut feature, "Primetime," starring Robert Pattinson as Chris Hansen, the host of the series "To Catch a Predator." The film revisits the years from 2004 to 2007, when the show broadcast on "Dateline NBC" organized sting operations against potential pedophiles.

What changes in your pocket when the media enters the scene

The feature film highlights Hansen's obsession with proving his supremacy on television, especially when the show was moved to a primetime slot, competing with high-rating series like "Lost." The pursuit of audience numbers raises questions about the ethics of exposing crimes in an entertainment format.

What changes in your pocket when the production clashes

The screenplay, written by Ajon Singh, shows the tension between Hansen and his producer, Andie Bender, played by Merritt Wever. While the host maintains the belief that his work has social utility, the producer seeks to maximize profits, generating a conflict of interest that reflects the reality of the film industry.

What changes in your pocket when the critics get involved

Chris Hansen, who did not participate in the production, criticized the film and bought advertisements before each screening, directing the audience to his streaming service TruBlu. He stated that he has never seen the feature and that he found Pattinson's performance "overly dramatic." Pattinson, for his part, responded that he "hopes Hansen likes the film."

What changes in your pocket when art becomes surreal

The director uses different filming formats and a soundtrack by Ari Balouzian to create an atmosphere that blends reality and fiction, reflecting the duality between the pursuit of notoriety and the need for justice. The film's aesthetic makes the audience perceive the "holography" of contemporary media.

What changes in your pocket when critics receive the film

Publications like The Playlist and BBC praised Pattinson's performance, describing him as "extraordinary" and "magnetizing" in the role of Hansen. Critics recognized the film as a "scathing satire" of the reality television era, highlighting its black comedy tone and surrealist approach.

With information from The Playlist, BBC, Screen Daily.
